# parsec v5 — baseline arm `v5_b1_e1`

**Spec:** none — this arm characterises a rebuilt benchmark rather than testing a new optimizer design (see "Why v5 exists")
**Agent model:** `claude-sonnet-4-6`
**Optimizer model:** none — **no optimization step.** There is no seed/candidate/best/final lineage here, unlike [`v4_t_e1`](../../v4/v4_t_e1/summary.md) and [`v4_g_e1`](../../v4/v4_g_e1/summary.md)
**Budget:** `num_trials: 5, max_iterations: 0, max_usd: 50.0` per task (no optimizer budget — none was spent)
**Ledger:** [`results.json`](results.json), generated by [`../../../scripts/build_v5_b1_results_json.py`](../../../scripts/build_v5_b1_results_json.py) from the frozen [`source_v5_b1_e1.json`](source_v5_b1_e1.json)
**Heatmap:** [`../../../ui/heatmap_v5_b1_e1.html`](../../../ui/heatmap_v5_b1_e1.html) · **per-trial view:** [`../../../ui/trials_v5_b1_e1.html`](../../../ui/trials_v5_b1_e1.html)
**Recipes:** [`../../../recipes/v5/v5_b1_e1/`](../../../recipes/v5/v5_b1_e1/)
**Artifacts:** [`../../../artifacts/v5/seed/`](../../../artifacts/v5/seed/) — one shared bundle, the original skill, identical across all 136 tasks
**Per-task reports:** [`../../../reports/v5/v5_b1_e1/`](../../../reports/v5/v5_b1_e1/) (`<task>.md`, 136 files)
**Cost/time:** [`cost_time/`](cost_time/) (`v5_b1_e1_results_table.md`)

## The one-line result

**Mean reward 0.7260** across all 136 tasks, 0 errored trials, 0 missing. 30 tasks saturate at
1.0; 106 have headroom. **92 of 136 tasks (68%) are non-deterministic** — the single most
consequential fact here for anyone designing the optimizer arms that follow.

## Why v5 exists, and what this arm's skill actually is

v4's 34-task set and h4's 30-task held-out set were both found to have drifted from the copies
this branch's own `v4_t4_e1`/`v4_t4_e2`/`h4_t1_e1`/`h4_t1_e3` tables were built against (different
`golden.json`, seeds, and `verify.py` in several tasks). Rather than reconcile that lineage, v5 is a
from-scratch rebuild: new task copies under a `bench-v5-` prefix, no shared content with any v4/h4
tree, pooling two independently authored 68-task drops into **136 tasks**.

This arm's skill is **verified byte-identical (8/8 prompt files) to parsec commit `28e2c40`'s
`config/prompts/`**, checked against a fresh clone of the parsec reference repo, and equally
byte-identical to this branch's own [`artifacts/v4/seed/`](../../../artifacts/v4/seed/). That
verification matters because of what it caught:

> **A previous run of this same sweep was discarded.** `v5_t1_e1` (68 tasks) was run against a
> skill that turned out to be byte-identical to
> [`artifacts/v4/v4_g_e1/rejected/cand_0001`](../../../artifacts/v4/v4_g_e1/rejected/cand_0001) —
> a candidate produced by v4's **global optimizer** arm, which had been left installed in the live
> parsec clone's working tree (parsec's git HEAD still read `28e2c40`, so `git status` alone would
> not have shown it) and was inherited when the v5 benchmark tree was built from that clone. It was
> never a baseline. On the 68 tasks shared with this arm it inflated the mean by **+0.151**
> (0.7372 → 0.8885), moving several near-floor tasks to perfect — e.g.
> `cloud-024-guid-to-account` 0.200 → 1.000, `platform-005-wrong-owner-trap` 0.258 → 1.000.
> `cand_0001` scored 0.9274 on v4's own 34 tasks against a 0.8488 seed, so the inflation is exactly
> what an accepted-but-not-best optimizer candidate should look like.
>
> The lesson is cheap to carry forward: **pin the artifact under test to a verified commit, and
> verify it, rather than copying whatever a live working tree happens to hold.**

## The two task sets are statistically indistinguishable

v5 pools `v5_2026-10-10` ("10-10") and `v5_2026-10-12` ("10-12"). Task ids do not collide, and the
category mix is identical in both (10 cloud / 10 cost / 13 icinga / 35 platform). Membership is
recorded per task in the ledger's `task_set` field, from
[`task_set_10-12.txt`](task_set_10-12.txt).

| metric | 10-10 (68) | 10-12 (68) | all (136) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| mean reward | 0.7372 | 0.7149 | **0.7260** |
| median | 0.8000 | 0.7743 | 0.7867 |
| sd across tasks | 0.2698 | 0.2362 | 0.2529 |
| saturated (= 1.0) | 24 | 6 | 30 |
| unsaturated (< 1.0) | 44 | 62 | 106 |
| mean of unsaturated | 0.5938 | 0.6873 | 0.6485 |
| genuine zeros | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| **variable-reward tasks** | **38 (55.9%)** | **54 (79.4%)** | **92 (67.6%)** |
| deterministic | 30 | 14 | 44 |
| mean spread (variable only) | 0.6986 | 0.3938 | 0.5197 |
| mean sd (variable only) | 0.2890 | 0.1610 | 0.2139 |
| mean sd (all tasks) | 0.1615 | 0.1279 | 0.1447 |
| cost | $35.00 | $50.80 | $85.80 |

**Difference in mean: +0.0223** (10-10 minus 10-12) · SE 0.0435 · t = 0.51 · two-sided
permutation test **p = 0.62** (20 000 resamples). No detectable difference in overall difficulty,
so the two drops can be pooled and split randomly for a later train/test partition without
biasing it.

**One structural difference the mean hides**, and it matters for gating rather than for difficulty:
10-10 has 24 saturated tasks to 10-12's 6, while 10-12 varies more often (79% vs 56%) with a
*smaller* spread when it does (0.394 vs 0.699). 10-10 scores more all-or-nothing; 10-12 awards
finer partial credit. A random split will therefore mix two scoring textures — fine for a
difficulty-matched partition, worth remembering when reading per-task deltas.

## Stochasticity, and the noise floor it sets

**92 of 136 tasks (67.6%) return a different reward across identical repeated trials.** Mean
per-task trial sd is 0.1447; among the variable tasks alone it is 0.2139, with a mean min-to-max
spread of 0.5197. The [per-trial view](../../../ui/trials_v5_b1_e1.html) draws every trial so this
is visible rather than averaged away.

| quantity | value | what it bounds |
|---|--:|---|
| mean per-task trial sd | 0.1447 | raw run-to-run noise |
| SE of a 5-trial task mean | 0.0647 | precision of one task's score |
| 95% CI half-width, per task | 0.1268 | per-task claims |
| **min detectable per-task delta** | **~0.25** | one task's before/after at n=5 |
| SE of the 136-task suite mean | 0.0217 | suite-level claims |

**Consequence for the optimization arms that follow.** A per-task improvement smaller than roughly
**0.25** cannot be distinguished from run-to-run noise at 5 trials — so a hill-climb gate that
accepts a candidate on any per-task gain **will accept noise**, and will do so on two thirds of
this benchmark. The suite mean is about 6× better resolved (SE ≈ 0.02), so pooled movement of
~0.06 upward is real. Either gate on suite-level movement, or raise trials per task for the gate
specifically. This is the same failure mode `reports/README.md` already documents for v1/v2 —
"read no cell without the `n` beside it" — now quantified for v5.

## By category

From `results.json`'s `sections.by_category` — do not hand-edit these:

| category | n | mean | saturated | variable | mean sd |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| platform | 70 | 0.7840 | 21 | 44 (63%) | 0.1032 |
| icinga | 26 | 0.6536 | 2 | 21 (81%) | 0.1836 |
| cloud | 20 | 0.5886 | 3 | 13 (65%) | 0.1888 |
| cost | 20 | 0.7547 | 4 | 14 (70%) | 0.1952 |

Platform is both the largest category and the least noisy (sd 0.103); icinga, cloud and cost all
sit near 0.19, roughly double that. Since platform is 70 of 136 tasks, the pooled mean sd of 0.145
is pulled down by it — a train/test split that happened to concentrate platform tasks on one side
would land different noise characteristics on each half, which is a second reason to split
randomly and then check the realised split rather than assuming it.

## Data-quality notes

1. **Zero errored trials across all 680.** Four tasks needed a re-run to get there: two
   (`icinga-010-stuck-anarchysubjects`, `icinga-201-soft-critical-not-yet-hard`) hung for ~6.5h on
   an intermittent gateway `httpx.ConnectTimeout` that nothing above it enforced a deadline on; two
   (`platform-002-collection-not-found-rca`,
   `platform-113-account-region-override-not-capacity`) completed with 2 of 5 trials errored, so
   their means were computed off 3 valid trials. All four were re-run clean before this ledger was
   vendored; `build_v5_b1_results_json.py` asserts `errored_trials == 0` on every task and would
   refuse to generate otherwise.
2. **The 2 genuine zeros are not errors.** `cloud-304-marketplace-active-past-end` and
   `icinga-072-alert-output-not-decoy-metrics` both score 0.0 with `errored_trials: 0`, on all five
   trials — the skill answered and was wrong every time, which is a result, not an infra failure.
   Neither is yet investigated; both are worth a read before the optimizer arms, since a task that
   is deterministically 0 is either a real capability gap or a contract defect.
3. **Trial timeouts are not enforced end-to-end.** The adapter's 20-minute per-trial cap did not
   fire on the two hung tasks above; the hang sat below it. Worth fixing before the optimizer arms,
   which will run far more trials.

## Next moves

- Randomly split these 136 into a train half (`o5`) and a held-out half (`h5`). The permutation
  test above is what licenses a random split rather than a drop-based one.
- Run the task-by-task (`t`) and global (`g`) optimizer arms on `o5`, validate on `h5`.
- **Decide the gating rule first**, given the noise floor above — this is the open question this
  arm exists to surface.
